title: Been working on a game for a good ~4 months now with 2x Ultra subs. It just absolutely blows me away Claude is able to build beautiful scenes even better than me, an experienced developer, entirely off math alone
author: duffmanhb

comments.author: duffmanhb
comments.body:
Here's [another pic](https://imgur.com/a/jYPHEr9) that I pushed to the limits but didn't make the cut because real time rendering for the one on the right wouldn't work on lower end GPUs, but I'm still blown away.

The reason it's been taking so long, is well, I don't want to build slop. So MOST of my tokens go into training the model, building the harness, creating skills, and the constant struggle fest on teaching AI what is "taste". Like what makes something resonate and look good. 

That's easily been the hardest because it's all intuition, so I personally have to do a lot of thinking and figure out how to communicate things. And the challenge is, some things are so self evident I'll even forget that it's core to the design process. 

Then you have things like the model just doing things wrong, fighting with it, insisting something's not right with X process, and it insisting it's something else, only to find out it is in fact X, and it was wrong, and wasted tons of time. 

I've had to partial reboot about 3 times, which each pseudo fresh itteration taking what we learned from the last and implimenting it going forward. 

But as of now I think we've got the formula down, a good 3 months later which equates to about ~15k in tokens. 

But what blows me away is that while there's visual checks, the actual building of everything is done entirely by math. By it writing code to build things. It's just so... alien. And not only that, but the next model is going to get even better, which means MOST of what I've been struggling to teach it and improve on, is likely going to be useless and unnecesary with the next major update as it's able to do it all without my help. I've already seen the new capabilities of Astra's next release. 

Which kind of makes me sad knowing it's all kind of wasted, but it's still a really fun project to reimagine and bring to life an old 90s game, for the modern era, with modern game theory and visuals in place. It's fun, and well, cheaper than a drug habbit lol

replies.author: duffmanhb
replies.body:
This is a zoomed out look of a small city. It's a much larger map. Inspired off one of my favorite games as a child, Ultima Online. Which is a fantasy MMO open world sandbox. 

They don't make them like that any more. But UO was basically the first proper MMO, but there was no proper linear game. you just sort of got dropped into the game, built your character and chose your path, and just kind of created your own adventure however you wanted to. It isn't like modern MMOs where you have regions that you progressively get into, then hit the end game grind. 

Since it's a sandbox, there's a huge focus on community, groups doing different types of events, all sorts of different professions, the economy/trading parts of it are huge and entirely player ran, real estate is essential since player houses are built through the whole world. Like being a "scammer" was literally a playing style people can choose to do. Some would just do normal theft, of stealing out of your bag, or bait some player into an ambush to loot his rares he thought he was coming to trade, and even exploiting in game mechanics to get in edge and trick someone into a bad trade. It was a legit playing style. 

Since the game had no real defined goals, "status" was a lot about it. Which is what made the economy so important. Having "rare" armor just looked nice, and wasn't reserved for super elite top tier end game players... But rather people who win events, hard challenges, exotic loot, etc. 

I've always had the UO itch, but every time I go back to it, it just still feels too old. It was great for the time but it never caught up with modern game techniques, so everyone's still using janky addons and workarounds to make an old system still playable. 

So I'm hoping to sort of revive that feeling of having an open world, sandbox MMO, that had a real economy underpinning everything, while also fun balanced combat for PvP and PvE
